ads.body: Why I include magnesium from @muscleblaze in my routine.
ads.transcript: I work long hours, I weight train and I run regularly. And even though I'm very conscious about the food intake that I have, completing every single micronutrients every single day is just not guaranteed. And magnesium is one of them. So I take magnesium supplement not because it is some sort of a magical supplement, but to make sure that I am not falling short of it for a longer period of time. Because deficiency in magnesium can impact normal muscle functions and nerve signaling, which can affect both my work and my training. And secondly, whatever small amount of hours I get to sleep, I want to optimize it. Adding magnesium can improve sleep quality. And regarding the brand, I personally use Muscle Blaze Magnesium Matrix. One, it do not source its magnesium from cheap form. In fact, it uses four different forms to source its magnesium. And secondly, I have said this number of times, Muscle Blaze take quality and testing very seriously, which is something that I value the most. So if you're planning to add magnesium in your diet plan, I would highly recommend to check out Muscle Blaze website. and I'm sure you won't be disappointed.

Code: MBDRADITI
We often talk about protein, carbs, and calories when it comes to fitness.

But recovery isn’t just about macronutrients. Micronutrients matter too.

Magnesium plays an important role in muscle function, energy production, nervous system health, and recovery. Whether you’re lifting weights, running, or simply staying active, it’s working behind the scenes every day.

That’s why I pay attention not just to how much I train, but also to how well I recover.

What’s one recovery habit you swear by? 👇
ads.transcript: Everyone talks about protein when it comes to recovery, but recovery doesn't come with protein alone. When we talk about performance and recovery, magnesium is one of the nutrients that often gets left out of the conversation. Every time your body moves, lifts, runs, produces energy, contracts a muscle or transmits signals through the nervous system, magnesium plays a crucial role in that process. This magnesium matrix by MuscleBlaze is super interesting. Instead of relying on a single form of magnesium, it combines four different sources. Magnesium bisglycinate, malate, L-threonate and aquamine. 2 tablets of this provide 440 mg of elemental magnesium. I take 1 tablet as per my daily requirement to support muscle recovery, energy levels, nervous system balance and sleep quality. So if you are someone who trains regularly and wants to optimize the basics, magnesium is definitely a nutrient worth paying attention. Get your magnesium matrix from MuscleBlaze.com now!

But I stuck through it all, and after a solid first trip, I took the stage. And during this whole time, Muscle Blaze was a constant. And Biozyme Performance Way was my go-to. ads.transcript: 21 days, 7 challenges, 1 stronger version of yourself. If you are a Naruto fan, then let's see how many you can complete. Challenge 1, do strength training for 4-5 days in a week. If you don't have gym, then work out at home. Challenge 2, do cardio for 30 minutes daily. Walking, cycling or skipping, anything that you enjoy. Challenge 3, limit junk food and eat a daily balanced nutritious meal. Challenge 4, do stretching and mobility for 10 minutes daily. Strength and flexibility are also important. Challenge 5, do meditation for 10 minutes daily and replace your bad habits. Challenge 6, choose a new skill and practice it for 30 minutes daily. ads.body: MuscleBlaze x Naruto is back! And a quick throwback to Japan 🇯🇵 with Saket. A trip that comes once in a lifetime 🤞🏻
ads.transcript: Last year, I went to Japan to take part in a beginner bodybuilding show. And there was a trip that I will never forget. So when Muscle Blaze told me that its Naruto collab was coming back, I knew I had to be a part of it. Now I have grown up watching Naruto, and his never give up attitude is something I swear by. Now ups and downs have been there in my journey. December 2023 was when I started, and then a year later when things were picking up, there was a fracture. And then some weight gain came with it. But I stuck through it all, and after a solid first trip, I took the stage. And during this whole time, Muscle Blaze was a constant. And Biozyme Performance Way was my go-to. In one scoop of its Rocky Road Fudge flavor, you'll get 25 grams of clean protein that's clinically proven to absorb higher compared to regular whey and it's easy on the gut. Muscle Blaze always blind tests its products and it's certified by Informed Choice UK, Lab Boy USA and Trustified World India. Now this is a limited edition version so along with it, a free Naruto shaker will also come. So don't miss the drop and check it out on muscleblaze.com right now.

ads.body:
Training smarter, not just harder for @hyroxindia Mumbai.

Focusing on station efficiency. Sharpening the run splits. And during race week, cutting volume while keeping intensity. And fuelling with a carb + protein combo my gut actually thanks me for. 

@cosmixwellness has been on this journey with me. And this Indonesian Cacao flavour, tastes so well that I look forward to having my protein.

See you at Hyrox, Mumbai !
.

#running #recovery #protein #hyrox
ads.transcript: I lost my High Rocks Delhi podium by 3 seconds. 3 seconds would have been saved anywhere. I kept replaying the race in my head. Every run, every station, every transition. And that made me realize, performance is built long before race day. So this time, I'm training smarter. I'm focusing on stations where I lost time. I'm reducing my training volume before race day. And I'm focusing a lot more on my recovery, especially my protein. That's why you will find Cosmix 100% fermented yeast protein in my bag. With 24 grams of protein, it is gut-friendly, has way-level absorption, and a complete amino acid profile. And this Indonesian cacao flavor makes me look forward to having my protein. I've trained hard. I'm recovering better. See you at Herox Mumbai.

ads.transcript: I was 90 kgs and now 71. And if you're a vegetarian struggling to increase your protein intake, here are 5 things that will help you. Comment protein for my vegetarian weekly protein planner that will help you hit 100 grams of protein per day. Number 1. Protein quality matters. Your body needs 9 essential amino acids to build and repair muscle, but some vegetarian food are often missing one or two of these important pieces. The simple fix pairs them smartly. Try an edamame keema pesto risotto, beetroot chana hummus with a seeded sado or a rajma falafel bowl with rice tabole. Number 2. Don't have a carb-only breakfast. Simple carbs on their own can leave you hungry again very quickly. Add protein, healthy fats and fiber to make breakfast more balanced. Try a chafala kuri on sado or my everyday double kokor piramisu frappe made with the whole truth plant protein. That's 25 grams of protein before even the day starts. Number three, protein needs a fiber-rich plate around it. Protein helps repair muscle, whereas fiber keeps your digestion moving and helps you stay full for longer. Try a Mediterranean salad with roasted beetroot, feta and chickpeas, aloo toque sweet potato chaat or Greek yogurt with berries, chia seeds and nuts. Just increase the fiber slowly and drink enough water. Number four, dessert can be high protein and still feel indulgent and nutritious. I make a dark chocolate protein mousse that is genuinely mind-blowing. My parents are obsessed with my saffron pistachio protein shrikhand made with the whole truth badam pista plant protein. Number 5, Sundays are for meal prep. Prepare a few protein bases like harissa paneer, gochujang, tofu and bhuna soya. During the week, turn them into wraps, bowls or salads.

They even let me get hands-on to make my own personalized bar. Honestly, we should all tag the whole truth in the comment below and convince them to do a limited edition Natasha drop. They chose a 6-month shelf life for freshness over the industry standard of over 12 months for convenience. Most brands demand your trust. The whole truth earned it. posts.creator: nikunjbiyani92
posts.caption: We improved our packaging after getting approval from the people who matter the most. Our customers.
posts.transcript: Ever since we launched Yeast Protein, we've received a lot of love for the product, but we did receive some hate for the packaging. Yeast Protein has a slightly lower bulk density, so the powder would tend to get stuck in the Ziploc, not allowing it to seal properly. But because we were so in love with just how beautiful this pouch looked, we spent the next six months just finding solutions within the pouch and came up with this, which was a pouch in pouch, only to find out that it creates other issues. Ultimately, we took the hard decision of moving to jars. They get the job done really well. So well that we saw a 15% increase in revenue just by moving from pouches to jars. All of this has been a cruel reminder to choose functionality over aesthetics, especially when it comes to packaging, and also to just listen to your consumer really, really carefully. So boy, am I glad that all those jarring comments about these pouches not functioning are behind us. And now all our variants and flavors are available in jars

tags.hook_line: We got hate for the packaging of our Yeast Protein
tags.summary: The creator explains packaging issues, reveals the switch to jars, and highlights the resulting sales lift.

posts.transcript: We all know that electrolytes are important, especially after an intense workout. But as a sports injury physiotherapist, there's one thing I always check when choosing an electrolyte drink. It's the sodium content. Human sweat contains 800 to 1200 mg of sodium per liter. So whether you're running, working out or cleaning in hot and humid conditions, you are losing this key electrolyte which helps in regulating your blood plasma volume and maintains the balance. So, if you replenish just with plain water, your body cannot retain that fluid. Your kidneys simply excrete it, leading to a state of cellular dehydration, muscle cramps, and brain fog. That's why Cosmic Hydration Mix contains 1000 mg of sodium per serving. It's an intentional dose designed for intense training days when you're sweating heavily. Along with sodium, you get 200 mg of potassium and 60 mg of magnesium, plus calcium, vitamin C, and zinc. to support your normal muscle function, bone strength and better immunity. And the best part it comes in flavors like Aam Panna Kala Khatta and Orange So the next time you sweating it out make sure your hydration keeps with you Thank you. Thank you.

posts.caption: Yes, we are going international! Guess where we are going first. 👀
posts.transcript: Why has TWT not gone international yet? The first reason is that the history of successful international expansions from Apple to Starbucks to Lululemon to Luckin Coffee suggests that building a dominant position in your home market is a necessary condition before you attempt a foreign market. Go too early and you might become dhobi ka kutta, na ghar ka na ghat ka. I explained this at length in my previous video. But there are two more reasons why an Indian clean label food brand should not go international. First, because hundred percent clean, natural food has low shelf life. Like our bars have three to six months of shelf life, whereas others have fifteen to eighteen months. What this means is we can't ship very far, and we definitely cannot afford delays in customs and port clearance. Any delay, and you have to write off the entire shipment. But an even bigger reason is that the developed world doesn't believe that Indian brands can do clean label. I once spoke with a top retailer of Singapore, and they were kind enough to actually tell me the truth. They said they loved our brand and our product, but clean label from India, mmm, who would buy that? That's something that comes from US or Europe or Australia. If you guys have something in Ayurveda or yoga, you give us that. But clean label, nah. This one obviously annoys me a lot because I personally know Americans, Europeans, Australians who've had our products and have told me that they haven't had anything this clean or this tasty in their home markets. And yet, how does one change this perception? Tell me, do you also have friends in the Western world that have told you the same? Please share it in comments. It'll give us the confidence we need to attempt this stupidity. And oh, did I mention that we are going to attempt this stupidity? I'll share more soon.

posts.creator: shashankfit
posts.caption: Some things are worth saying more than once ❤️  We’ve always believed that food is so much more than what it does to our bodies. It’s about who we share it with, the memories we make around it, and the joy of one more gujiya when Nani insists.  So we’re bringing this one back, because we feel just as strongly about it today as we did when we first said it.  Eat the sweets. Make the memories. Keep the good habits. And most importantly, enjoy the festivities.  Happy Diwali! 🪔
posts.transcript: My nani used to make the best mathris. Never once counted calories, never counted protein and macros. I don't think she knew what that word meant. But she did count other things like how many neighbours could she feed from one batch? 17. Every single Diwali. She counted how many years she'd been making them? 46. Six. Same recipe, same love. She counted how many festivals she saw her grandchildren at. And she made each one of them count. She counted the number of people at the table, the number of stories in the kitchen, the number of times someone said, BAS A KOR. She never knew the science behind food. But I think she knew what food was meant to do. To feed, to comfort, to connect. Now, we've turned food into maths, calories, macros, trackers, apps, and maybe on most days it works. But Diwali? Diwali was never meant to be about counting. It was meant to be about celebration of food, of people, of our culture. So this Diwali, let's not count the calories. Count the people, count the stories, count the blessings. Now don't get me wrong, I am not saying go all out and lose all those hard earned gains. I am just saying that food is as much about family and happiness as it is about nutrition. And maybe Diwali is a great time to let happiness be the primary objective. And that is the whole truth.

tags.hook_line: My nani used to make the best mathris.
benefits: reinforce brand philosophy of joy over numbers
tags.summary: A nostalgic story urges viewers to enjoy festive foods without obsessing over macros, aligning with the brand’s ethos.

posts.creator: shashankfit
posts.caption: Marketing will always need science. But without the art, it loses a little of its soul. And that’s the whole truth :)
posts.transcript: Marketing and brand building is becoming too much about metrics and maths, too much science and too little art. And I find that regrettable. I strongly believe that marketing is both art and science, left brain and right brain, logic and magic. But unfortunately, in this era of digital marketing and AI, I feel we are leaning too heavily on the side of logic, too much CPM and CTR and too little of how did that make you feel? Did it speak to you? Did it make you stop and think? Did it move you? Will it even stay with you? You know, a large part of it, I guess, is perhaps because marketing is run by MBAs, including me. And our overdeveloped left brains find enormous comfort in numbers. And so we shift all marketing monies to stuff that can be measured, leaving nothing for that which can only be fed. I mean, how do you measure returns on choosing that slightly greeny, matte texture on your pack that will give it a handmade feel? How will you measure ROI on a community event where 40 people take 4 hours on a Sunday to come ask the founder deeply thoughtful questions about the brand? And how will you ever justify writing, like physically writing letters to 50 people whose orders you screwed up? You can't, and so we don't. And that's sad because while marketing definitely needs science, without the art, the brand loses soul and it doesn't remain whole. And that's the whole truth.

tags.hook_line: Marketing and brand building is becoming too much about metrics and maths, too much science and too little art.
tags.summary: Explains why marketing needs both science and art to keep brands authentic.

posts.transcript: Real hazelnut flavor is not found in its crunch, it is found in its smell. In roasted hazelnut, more than 200 volatile aroma compounds were reported. Roast, Nutty Fat, Caramel, Dark Cocoa. Before understanding tongue sweetness, it is called nose. Actual Hazelnut. Now let's calculate Rs. 199. 55 grams of bar, 35% hazelnuts on the back. posts.caption: You often ask us how we manage to make our bars last so long without any preservatives. Here’s the whole truth.
posts.transcript: If you don't put any preservatives, how do your bars last five to six months? That's a very common question I get, so let me explain. To make hundred percent natural food last long, you need to do three things: reduce moisture, reduce oxygen, and start fresh. Let me tell you how we do all three. First, we work with dry fruits, right? Like that's cashews behind me, almonds, dates. Individually, all these dry fruits last over a year because they are inherently dry. Low moisture means low spoilage. Next, we try and use raw material that is as fresh as possible. You can make this bar with a date or a cashew that is two months old or a year old, and that would significantly affect both the taste and the shelf life of the bar. And last, you see this puffiness? We nitro flush our bars. Microorganisms, just like human beings, need both water and oxygen to live. So if we fill the packet with nitrogen, which we put in at pressure, it displaces the oxygen. That's why you see that our packs are a little puffed. The bar hasn't spoiled. It's nitrogen that is keeping it from getting spoiled because it's removed all the oxygen. So yeah, these three simple things, which are simple but not easy, done day in and day out by a dedicated staff that's committed to making the best food for your family because this is our whole truth.

posts.creator: shashankfit
posts.caption: The truth is, fear travels faster than facts.  The whole truth is, transparent brands lose when the facts never reach consumers.  How do we make the truth easier to find?
posts.transcript: Fear travels faster than facts on social media. Let me give you a live example. Last week, someone raised a concern about a whey protein on Reddit. They pointed out that the cholesterol values on the pack had changed and so had the whey that we declare lecithin. They also added that in their latest batch of whey, it foamed a bit more than the last one. And then they correlated these two observations and inferred that this must mean that TWT has downgraded its protein quality and quietly changed the pack without being transparent about it. Now, their observations were correct, but the inference was not. We never have and never will touch quality. In fact, that's the reason why prices are rising. Because we refuse to use the cheap varieties of whey that are so easily available in the market. The gap between the observation and the inference was due to a lack of context. So, as always, we shared context. we posted a detailed response to each of their points. The OP acknowledged the response and asked the moderators to pin it. All of this happened within a few hours. Yet a week later today the OG post has over 4000 likes while our comment has barely 50 This is the fundamental problem of how social media algos are built See there was no bad actor in this play, the OP had a valid concern, we had a valid answer and we replied super quick. And yet, it's fair to assume that over 90% of the people who read the post never saw our response and most probably never will. This is same by the way with influencer videos. So many times in the past, an ill-informed influencer has made an accusatory video, we responded with facts and 2 days later the influencer went and deleted the video without any explanation. I assume it's because they figured they were wrong. But by then the damage was done. The video had already reached lakhs of views and our comment barely a few thousand. As someone trying to build an honest brand, this makes me wonder how to fight this attention-seeking algo, one that loves spreading fear more than facts, where an accusation or even a simple question travels far more than the answer. And in the court of public law, the matter gets settled without one side even getting a hearing. In such a world, how does one tell their whole truth? Do you have any ideas? I'd love to know.

tags.hook_line: Fear travels faster than facts on social media.
tags.summary: The creator highlights how rumors spread faster than facts and showcases the brand’s transparent, rapid response to protect its whey product.

posts.creator: shashankfit
posts.caption: Ever wondered why your protein bar packet puffs up?  Because we nitro-flush them. We replace most of the oxygen in the pack with nitrogen, which helps protect ingredients like nuts from oxidation, keeps the bar tasting fresher for longer, and slows down microbial growth too.  All this from an inert gas you’re breathing as you read this.  Nitrogen might just be the most natural preservative that’s all around us but we can’t see it. And that’s the whole, nitro truth.
posts.transcript: My bar is all puffed up. Has it gone bad? No. This is nitrogen flushing. Let me explain. We make our bars with just a few natural ingredients. Cashews, almonds, dates, that sort of stuff, right? But then how do we achieve a shelf life of six months? One of the ways in which we do it is by nitro flushing our bars. You see, food goes bad when microbial growth in it exceeds a certain limit. and microbes just like human beings need oxygen to survive and grow. You see this packing machine behind me at the time of packing this small nozzle here this small nozzle inserts nitrogen into the pack at high pressure and that displaces the oxygen inside the packet. No oxygen means no oxidation and bacterial growth slows down dramatically. Simple. By the way nitrogen is inert so it doesn't affect the taste or the texture or anything else in the bar. And oh, did you know that 78% of the air that we breathe is already nitrogen? So yeah, it's totally safe and this is a globally followed best practice. Oh, and last thing, you might notice that the bar puffs up even more at high altitudes or in an aircraft. That's because at altitude, the air pressure outside the pack drops significantly. The pressure inside the pack where nitrogen was sealed at ground level stays the same. So the pack expands outwards to equalize. Same reason why your ears pop on a plane. Same reason why a sealed water bottle crumples when you land. Rest assured, your bar is safe and good. It's being preserved by the most natural preservative that you're breathing right now, nitrogen. And that's the whole puffy truth.

tags.hook_line: My bar is all puffed up. Has it gone bad?
tags.summary: Explains how nitrogen flushing keeps protein bars fresh and safe.

posts.caption: Natural flavours are NOT natural. There, we said it.
posts.transcript: The whole truth is that natural flavors are not natural. Let me explain. Say you see natural vanilla flavor on a pack. You may think, oh, okay, real vanilla. No. All this natural means is that the starting material of this ingredient came from something in nature. And in the case of vanilla flavor, that starting material is often wood. To make it, you take waste wood from paper mills, break it down chemically until you isolate just one molecule. Vanillin. That's the one molecule that gives vanilla its main taste. And because wood comes from nature, this is legally natural flavor, even though the processing is as industrial as any artificial flavor. Now, why do brands do this? Because, hey, real vanilla is extremely expensive. A vanilla orchard takes months to grow. The beans have to be hand pollinated and harvested and dried for weeks. Wood waste costs nothing. And of course, natural flavor makes the product sound healthy. So the next time you see natural flavors on a pack, just know that you're buying lab-made molecules, not the plant. There's nothing natural about it and that's just the whole truth.

tags.hook_line: The whole truth is that natural flavors are not natural.
tags.summary: Explains why natural vanilla flavor is actually lab-made and not truly natural.

posts.creator: shashankfit
posts.caption: Thankfully, times are changing. Fit is the new sexy. A lot of my friends now spend more on what they eat than what they wear. If this continues, we might see spot a few Food unicorns in the next decade.  PS: I’m sure I haven’t covered all the reasons. Do share in comments. And tell me if you disagree - I want to learn.
posts.transcript: Zomato, Paytm, Nykaa, Mama Earth, Physicswala, Lenskart. Just a few of the unicorn IPOs of the last decade. Do you know what else is common to all of them? None of them is a packaged foods company. I asked Claude to find me packaged food companies from the last decade that IPO'd at a billion dollar valuation. It could find one. Bikaji Foods started in the 1980s. Not one new age packaged food brand started in the last two decades has listed at a billion dollars. Not one. There are many reasons why, but I think that the core reason is gross margin. The money that you have left after subtracting cost of making the product from its selling price. Personal care brands make 70% gross margin. Apparel, similar. Beauty can go up to 80%. Food, 40% if you're lucky. Unilever's skincare business, 70% margin. Unilever's food business, just about 40% gross margin. That's why they've sold their entire foods business. At that margin, it just didn't make sense. Basically, we humans don't like paying high for food. We are happy to pay 5000 bucks for a perfume or 1000 bucks for a face cream that's largely water, costs about 100 to make and comes in a glass bottle that costs more than the product inside. But we think twice about spending 100 bucks for a protein bar made with real almonds real dates real whey all of that good stuff But why is that I think it because we value how we look outside more than how we feel inside Everything that we can flaunt, a sexy bag, great clothes, fancy shoes, we are happy to spend a bomb on. But anything that we consume in private, like a biscuit or a bar, nah, nothing to show off here. Low prices means low gross margin, which means that after cost of goods and logistics and retailer margins and discounts, all you have is barely five bucks left for marketing. And that is the problem. How will you get new users? How will you tell more people and more people that you actually exist? How will you grow? The only way for food brands to grow is through word of mouth and great distribution. Make a stellar product, make it available widely and let consumers tell other consumers about it. This growth, of course, looks far slower than marketing burn-led growth, but it's the only sustainable way to make a food business and there are no shortcuts here. Of course, there are many other factors too. Low shelf life, which means a lot of wastage in food. The fact that taste preferences change every 100 kilometers in our country, so you can never really please everyone. And of course, insane competition. Every locality has their own bakery and their favorite cafe, selling everything from cookies to bread. But the biggest reason why packaged food brands don't grow as much or as fast as others, I believe, is low cross-margin. What do you think? Have you noticed this?

tags.hook_line: Zomato, Paytm, Nykaa, Mama Earth, Physicswala, Lenskart.
tags.summary: Discusses why packaged food companies struggle with margins and how protein bars fit into the new fitness trend.

Which is great news. Moms need whey for sure. But unfortunately, the world does not have enough whey protein. Three things have caused this. First, GLP-1s. Yes, Ozempic, Monjaro, VigoVe. All these miracle weight loss drugs. Well, turns out when you lose that much weight, you lose muscle too. So every patient is being told to take whey protein because whey really is the gold standard of protein supplements. Estimates suggest that 12 to 15% of America has tried GLP-1s already. That's over 3 crore users in one country alone. And now that patents are coming off, developing countries like India will see a GLP-1 explosion and with it a protein demand explosion. Second, every brand wants a piece of that protein trend. Protein is now in everything. From chips to ice cream to protein cake and samosas. It's mad. And where do you think all this protein is coming from? Mostly whey. Last, supply. You see, whey is a byproduct of cheese making. And cheese consumption globally is actually declining. So the input is getting scarce. not to mention it takes over a thousand crores and more than two years to set up a way processing plant so factories that are coming online today are still reacting to demand signals from two years ago and the world has completely changed in these two years so supply just can't catch up it's for all of these reasons that way costs have increased by four times in two years and there is no end in sight. Nobody could have planned for this and it's sad but that's just the truth.

posts.caption: Food is NOT software. It isn’t winner take all. It isn’t ‘try fast fail fast’. And it isn’t a sprint.   It’s a marathon. Slow and steady wins the 20 year race. That’s something most VCs don’t like to hear. But what to do - it is the whole truth.   PS: As a wise man @arjunpurky once said - the way to build a Fast Moving Consumer Goods company, is slowly.
posts.transcript: We've raised over 600 crores in venture capital as a food company. And I can tell you that most VCs do not understand food companies. Because the entire VC playbook was built in the Silicon Valley. It was built for software. And food is not software. Three big differences, right? One, there is no winner-take-all in food. In tech, one player captures the entire market. Google, Facebook, Uber or Ola, Swiggy or Zomato, one winner or maximum two takes it all. Food does not work like that. In fact, FMCG does not work like that. Take oral care in India, for example. One of the rare categories where the market leader, Colgate, has greater than 50% market share. But even here, the remaining 50s split amongst so many other brands like Dabur, Patanjali, Pep Sudden, Closeup, Sensodyne, plus a ton of regional players. You don't have to be number one to survive. You don't have to give stupid discounts to acquire consumers at any cost. The number 10 player will also make a great business. 2. You cannot try fast and fail fast in food. fast and break things. That a great idea when the thing that you breaking is a feature It a terrible idea when the thing that you breaking is consumer trust In tech you can ship a half feature over the air and see how it flies. But in food, if I launch a half-tested bar and you don't like the taste or worse, it's unsafe, my brand is dead. Food companies get one shot. We have to get it right the first time. And hence, we do spend a lot more time perfecting the product before we ship it. Now that might make us look slow, but we're not because, and this is point number three, food is a marathon. It is not a sprint. Tech companies can scale from zero to a billion dollars in like three years, but consumer products businesses are compounding businesses. They grow steadily over 20, 30, 40 years. and that's the magic of compounding right a 600 crore top line business which is by the way what we are today growing at just 15 percent year on year for the next 20 years will make us a 10,000 crore business but to see that future we have to stay alive and to stay alive we must never break your trust. And that means being slow and deliberate about our choices. And hey, most VCs would not like that. But that's just the whole truth.

benefits: Positions food as a marathon business

posts.caption: “30+ vitamins & minerals” sounds like the responsible choice for your kid, no?  That’s exactly what the label wants you to feel. Because here’s what it doesn’t say: Most of those “vitamins & minerals” aren’t coming from real food. They’re added back in. They’re synthetic and lab-made, added post ultra-processing, to compensate for what was stripped out in the first place.  So the product gets to look nutritious on paper.  But your kid’s body? It doesn’t read nutrition labels. It responds to how nutrients are delivered, absorbed, and actually used. Most of these lab-made additions don’t quite w
posts.transcript: This is [beep]. This does not increase immunity. And no, this does not give you stronger bones. Yes, these drinks do have nutrients, but they’re mostly useless because most of it is just peed out by your child. Let me explain. Say the label promises 300 mg of calcium. Your child drinks it, calcium hits their gut. [burp] Now, for the calcium to actually build bones, it needs to get absorbed into the bloodstream. But here’s the problem. Calcium competes with magnesium for absorption. When both show up together in high doses, like they do in these drinks, they block each other. Your body can only process so much at once. So from that 300 mg of calcium, maybe just 90 mg gets absorbed. The rest, straight to the toilet. And even the calcium that does get absorbed, it still can’t build bone on its own, because for that it needs vitamin D. So from the 300 mg of calcium, you’re lucky if even 30 gets used. And if you think this is just a calcium-magnesium problem, no. Too much zinc blocks iron. Iron competes with copper. Even vitamins fight with each other. But the food marketeer knows that when a parent sees these 30 vitamins and minerals on the label, they will buy it without realizing that most of it just went out as pee. Because our bodies are designed to absorb nutrition from whole foods slowly. Calcium from ragi releasing through the morning, iron from dal coming in hours later, magnesium from real cocoa in small amounts. But the food industry does the exact opposite. They first process food so much that it loses most nutrition, and then hey, they add it all back as a chemical dump of 30 isolated lab-made vitamins and minerals to make these tall claims. What a great solution to a problem that they only created. How stupid. And that is the whole truth.

tags.summary: The creator debunks kid vitamin drinks, highlighting absorption issues and urging whole‑food nutrition.

posts.caption: That cartoon character is NOT your child’s friend.   It’s despicable. Young kids can’t read intent. Food marketers know this. So they send in cartoons and mascots - characters designed to earn trust. And then they use that trust to sell sugar.  So next time your kid picks up a box because of the cartoon on it… stop. Flip it. Read. You WILL feel like the bad guy. Sadly, someone has to be. But remember, that cartoon isn’t your child’s friend. It’s a mascot with a sales target.  And that’s the whole truth.
posts.transcript: This is the single most amoral, manipulative and downright dirty thing that food marketers do. This bunny is not your child's best friend. But your child doesn't know that. Because children under 8 cannot recognize persuasive intent. They literally cannot understand that an ad is trying to sell them something. So when our kids see this cartoon character, they don't see marketing. They see a friend, a real friend. And food marketers know this and exploit it on purpose. They build entire fictional worlds around these mascots. Chocolate jungles, superhero team-ups, TV shows, games, all designed to deepen that bond. So when this friend tells your child, hey, eat this for breakfast every morning, it's great for you. Your child believes it because friends don lie right That is the trap And the next time when you say no to a serial that 50 sugar you the villain And that cartoon rabbit is the hero That is the strategy Because once your child bonds with that mascot, the marketeer has turned your child into their salesman. By the way, there are countries that are banning this. Like Chile. By the mid-2010s, nearly half their children were overweight or obese. So in 2016, they acted. Banned cartoons on junk food packaging, added warning labels, kicked junk food out of schools. The result? Purchases of sugary drinks dropped by nearly 25%. Because when you remove the manipulation, behavior changes. But when there's a multi-billion dollar food industry on one side and a defenseless six-year-old on the other, it was never a fair fight. So remember, that cartoon character is not your child's friend. He is the enemy. And that is the whole truth.

tags.hook_line: This is the single most amoral, manipulative and downright dirty thing food marketers do.
tags.cta: Flip the package, read the label, be the ‘bad guy’

We will not secretly shrink pack sizes. And we will not stop using whole dates or real nuts i
posts.transcript: Dear lover of the whole truth bars, I'm afraid I have some bad news for you today. For the first time in our history, we are going to increase prices on our OG protein bars. Here's why. Rachu and I started TWT 7 years ago and our first product was this double cocoa protein bar. Just 5 ingredients, 12 grams of protein, priced at Rs. 100. 7 years later and nothing has changed. The same 5 ingredients, the same handmade process, the exact same bar. Cashews have doubled from Rs. 380 to Rs. 750 a kg. Cocoa has also doubled from Rs. 280 to Rs. 580. and whey protein concentrate has tripled from Rs. 700 to over 2000 kg. Food inflation in the last few years has been insane I sure you felt it in your kitchen and that exactly how we run our kitchen You know when cocoa doubled the industry shifted to using dark compound and cocoa substitutes. When weight tripled, people quietly changed their recipes and delivered lesser protein than promised. And hey, who even uses cashews and almonds and whole dates in their bars anymore? Well, we do. and we'd rather shut shop than deviate even an inch from our recipe, from our promise. So yeah, no option. We will have to increase prices on our bars by about 15 to 20%. posts.caption: NO “healthy” drink will make your kid taller.  Kids food marketing is broken. These ‘growth’ claims are designed to tap into a parent’s biggest fear: What if my child falls behind? What if I don’t do enough for them? So they sell big “clinically proven” claims.  The studies behind most of these claims? Often flawed. Just like the product itself, which are often junk loaded with 50% refined sugar(!!!!)  The whole truth is much simpler. ~80% of height is genetics. And for the rest, well, real growth comes from real food and environment. Not lab-made powders.
posts.transcript: This is not true. Neither is this. No healthy drink will make your kid taller. But they say it's clinically proven. Ah, let me tell you the whole truth. Certain brand has been milking that taller claim for nearly two decades. There is a 2006 study behind that claim. But in an interview, the lead scientist of the study told a journalist at The Print, it was primarily the milk that produced these results. Yup, the milk did the work, not the powder, which by the way is 50% sugar to get the kids addicted to it. And here's what makes it even worse. She also said, the study was performed only on children who otherwise had good nutrition. You see the problem now? They tested well-fed kids and the milk did the work. And they turned that into, our powder makes kids taller. Because they know every parent wants their kids to grow faster. In fact preying on parents anxiety has worked so well that even new age brands have copied this big food playbook and launched a height or a growth version of their milk mix. But please, don't get food. Here is what actually determines height. Around 80% is genetics, the DNA your child inherited from you. That's locked in. No food or powder or prayer can change that. Remaining 20% environment. And yes, nutrition is the biggest piece of that 20%. But nutrition doesn't mean powders with vague claims about supporting growth. It means daal, eggs, milk, roti with vegetables, fruit, real food. With protein, carbs and fats, your body actually recognizes, be it home or packaged food. So the next time you see a height claim on a drink, ask yourself, where's the research and what does it actually say? And what are the ingredients? Are they real food or some synthetic, lab-made stuff? Because your child's growth does not need marketing, it needs nutrition and that is the whole truth.

posts.caption: Have you come across brands that stand for completely different things but are from the same company? Tell me in comments - esp the ones that shocked you.

The biggest conglomerates proudly call themselves a house of brands. 30 years ago, fair skin was trending, so they had a brand. Today, real beauty is trending, they have a brand for that too. 10 years ago, extreme gym maxing was trending, they had a brand. Today, 100% clean protein is trending, they have a brand for that too. The same companies sell sugary cereals and healthy muesli, fried snacks and baked snacks, artificial and natural. Same parent company, just different brands. This is called a holding company and this strategy is called hedging. It's a very smart strategy. You don't need conviction. You just need coverage because whatever trend wins, you win. Now, here's the difference. At The Whole Truth, we don't have a holding company. We have a holding philosophy. If an ingredient doesn't belong in your body, it will never enter our factory under this brand or any other. Because there is no other brand. We will never launch a second brand that quietly uses the very ingredients that we publicly stand against. We don't hedge. We don't run a portfolio and we don't hide. Is that the smartest growth strategy? Maybe not. But it lets us look you in the eye and sleep well at night. And isn't that the whole point?

posts.caption: The untold history of milk-mixes.  Soldiers carried it to war. Explorers took it to Antarctica. So how did it become the sugar-loaded, synthetic cocktail kids drink today?  We went looking for answers.  This is the history (and the corruption) of the humble malt powder.  Watch. Learn. And if you like what you see, switch back to how it used to be. Link in bio. Use code HISTORYREPEATS for 10% off your first order.  Cheers,  Uncle Shashank
posts.transcript: This healthy kids drink is not real food, but it used to be. It used to be made with three simple ingredients. It used to be consumed by babies, mountaineers, and soldiers alike. But then what happened? How is it that today our kids are drinking this sugar loaded thirty ingredient chemical cocktail? Here's the whole truth. In the eighteen hundreds, malt-based drinks were considered nutritious. Doctors prescribed it to kids for easy energy. But there was one small problem, low shelf life. Until the Horlick brothers tried something crazy. They took malt, wheat, and milk and dried it in a vacuum. The result, a shelf-stable powder that wouldn't spoil for months, and they called it malted milk. Just three ingredients. Simple, right? Well, this simple mix was so effective that it found itself everywhere. Soldiers carried it to wars, explorers took it to Antarctica, and families hoarded it during the Great Depression. So brands saw an opportunity. They added sugar and chocolate to make it appeal to an even wider audience. That is how the modern day health food drink was born. It was a raging hit, but the food marketer wanted more. When malt brands came to India, they found an aspiring nation of parents who wanted their kids to excel at studies, excel at sports, and at everything in between. Life was a race, and no parent wanted their kid to be left behind. They figured that if they could tap into the dreams and the insecurities of the Indian parent, their products would sell better. So if iron deficiency was a concern, they added synthetic iron. If immunity was a worry, they packed in twenty random synthetic vitamins and minerals. If parents had anxiety about their kids' height, they made growth claims as if adding more chemicals would make the kids taller. And as competition grew, brands kept adding more so that they could promise even more. And just like that, we went from three clean ingredients to a thirty plus chemical cocktail nobody asked for. So how do we fix this? Today, the nutrition needs are different. Kids aren't lacking calories. They're lacking real food, and they're lacking protein. So we took some inspiration from history and rebuilt Food Drink. Food that you can drink with just seven clean ingredients. Real foods, real protein, real sweeteners, raised to the power of lactoferrin, a milk protein that supports iron absorption and immunity. Because, hey, that's all that kids need, and that is the whole truth.

tags.hook_line: This healthy kids drink is not real food, but it used to be.
tags.summary: The creator narrates the evolution of malt drinks to expose current sugary formulations and offers a discount to switch back.

And this surprised a lot of people. The comment section was full of, how is this even possible? They were shocked. And listen, I get your surprise. We are an expensive brand. We have insane brand love and word of mouth and hence actually we spend quite less. Then how? Is it the logistics costs or the salary costs? No we benchmarked all of them and we fairly efficient across the board Then what The answer is simple really real food is really expensive Take whey protein for example when we started two years ago we bought our first lot of whey concentrate for about 700 rupees a kg. The latest quote that we've got from suppliers is 2300 rupees a kg. That's tripling in two years. Now we've also increased our MRPs, yes, so we went from 3000 to 4000 rupees. But does that cover for the cost increase? Not even close. This is just one example. Similar stories are playing out across all agri commodities, from cocoa to cashew to everything in between. And as a brand that's committed to 100% real food, we have no alternative. We will never replace cocoa with dark compound. We won't replace real fruit with flavors or fruit powders and we'll never ever deliver lesser protein than we claim. So we are just left with two options, either increase prices or make a loss. And we've chosen to do a bit of both. And that's just the whole truth.

posts.caption: Heavy metals are a problem because unlike most things you eat, your body can’t break them down. So over time, they accumulate - in your kidneys, bones, even your brain.  But here’s what those scary headlines don’t tell you: presence doesn’t mean unsafe.  This is why regulatory safety limits exist. In India, FSSAI says chocolate is safe when it has less than 2.5 mg of lead per kg, and less than 1.5 mg of cadmium per kg. These are based on what our bodies can actually handle.  At TWT, we test every batch of our chocolate against these limits.  So enjoy your chocolate. The simple joy of it far ou
posts.transcript: Yes, dark chocolate can have heavy metals in it. But should you panic and stop eating it? Let me tell you the whole truth. There are two heavy metals of concern in dark chocolate. Cadmium and lead. Cadmium enters the chocolate from the cacao bean itself. When the cacao trees absorb nutrients and water, they also absorb cadmium if it's present in the soil. Lead enters later, during handling and processing of the cacao beans. Think dust settling on beans as they dry outdoors or contact with the machinery during grinding. But here's the part that everyone leaves out. Today's amounts of these elements exist naturally in our food. Rice has heavy metals, spinach has it, and yes, so does this coffee. That's just how our food system works. And that's absolutely okay, because our bodies can handle these small amounts just fine. And that's also the reason why government regulations set safety limits based on scientific research. In India, FSACI says chocolate is safe when it has less than 2.5 mg of lead per kg and less than 1.5 mg of cadmium per kg. If a lab test for a chocolate shows numbers below this threshold, the chocolate is completely safe. So, all you need to do is buy your chocolate from a brand that tests every batch and hey, eat in moderation. And then don't let fear mongering steal the joy of real chocolate from you. Because hey, that's the whole truth. you

posts.caption: Sharing vs Secrecy. What should a founder do?
posts.transcript: Every founder I know has this one fear. How much should I tell my people? Should I tell everyone what our strategy is? What our P&L is? Do all 250 people need to know how much money we burnt last month? What if one of them has a friend at a competitor or what if one of them leaves tomorrow and joins a competitor? And then there are even tougher questions like, you know, who all need to know what we are launching next or how much money we have left in the bank? And listen, this fear of leaks is quite warranted. It's happened to us in the past before we launched our dark chocolates, which are perhaps the world's first date sweetened dark chocolates. News leaked to a competitor and they went out and put an Instagram post and went and told retailers and customers that they're launching a similar product. And of course, the product never came because it's damn tough to make date sweetened chocolates. but you can imagine the amount of heartburn and turmoil and confusion it caused internally. So, knowing all of this, what do we do at TWT? Well, we share. We overshare. Let me show you something. So, every month we do a town hall where everyone gathers and we share everything from our P&L to our numbers to our strategy to the individual functional strategy. This is where everyone sits and this podium is where I go and stand You see the screen behind me this comes down and we put a presentation there and we lay everything bare And every time we do this, there's a voice in my head that's asking which one of my 250 people will leak something today? And when I know that someone will, why do I continue to do this? But then I think of the other 249 who will not do anything of that sort, who are getting so much more context about why we exist and how we are trying to achieve our mission. And I strongly believe that when you have more context, you get much better at your work. So that's why we do this. But there's more to this. This is clearly sensitive information, right? Like even a child would know that they can use this information to hurt TWT. and yet we choose to stand here every month and stand naked and tell everyone everything. It's our way of saying, listen, we trust you not to misuse it. And I think this vulnerability is the bedrock of building trust. Now, as you know, we are trying to rebuild the world's trust in its food. And we can't do that if we can't even build trust with our own people. So yeah, you know, despite all our fears, we share. Because to build the whole truth, our people need to know the whole truth. And that's the whole truth.

posts.caption: Excess of anything can throw the balance off, even foods marketed as “better for you.”
posts.transcript: Dates are having their main character moments but not all dates are good dates and you can't just wipe check this one because there's actual nutrition science involved. It depends on many factors. Is it whole dates? Are they powdered? Are they beaten into a syrup? Well all of them have a different fiber content and a very different glycemic index. But this is the true takeaway I want you to have that at the end of the day natural sugar is still sugar and the body will process it as sugar. So when you look at sugar don't look at just added sugars but total sugars because nutrition doesn't work in isolation. Good nutrition is all about balancing your macros. Everything else is just not. So the verdict? Dates aren't your will in, excess of them are. When our grandparents and parents said that excess of anything is bad, that's where they had it right.

posts.creator: gayatrichona
posts.caption: This is your cue to start seeing labels beyond the marketing!
posts.transcript: [upbeat music] In India, even a glucose biscuit can legally call itself healthy. Welcome back to The Nutrition Files. I'm Gayatri Chona, founder of Fab, a nutritionist and a mom of two. I overthink food for a living so you don't have to. And today, we are opening the file on labels, because what is being sold to you on the front and what's quietly confessing on the back, drastic difference. Here's what claims for high protein and multigrain look like. In India, for a food to be called high protein, it needs to be only eight grams per 100 calories. Multigrain, that's just 10% grains, and the rest can still be refined flour. And natural on the pack, well, that's not a nutritional standard at all. Coconut sugar is natural, but it still lands in your bloodstream with a glycemic index of 54 versus white sugar at 65. Your body barely notices this gap. Your body doesn't read labels. It processes how much of what you actually eat. Nutrition isn't just a standalone claim, but it needs to be looked at holistically. So the next time a product calls itself healthy, make sure to turn it around. [upbeat music]

tags.hook_line: In India, even a glucose biscuit can legally call itself healthy.
tags.summary: Gayatri breaks down deceptive Indian food labels and urges viewers to look beyond marketing.

posts.creator: gayatrichona
posts.caption: GLP-1 is the trend. Smart nutrition is the constant.
posts.transcript: India just handed 1.4 billion people an appetite-suppressing drug. But here's what this actually means for your body. Welcome back to The Nutrition Files. I'm Gayatri Chona, founder of FAB, a nutritionist and a mom of two. I overthink food for a living, so you don't have to. And today we're opening the hottest file in town, GLP-1. GLP-1 have revolutionized. GLP-1 is a very interesting molecule. We are in the beginning of the most effective medical intervention for obesity. This is transformational. GLP-1 is spreading fast. Clinics, prescriptions, and even dinner table conversations. But no one's asking the question that matters the most. How much protein are you actually getting when the appetite goes down? Because here's what happens. GLP-1 suppresses appetite, so you eat fewer calories. When that happens, without enough protein, your body burns muscle and not just fat. And here's the catch. On GLP-1, your appetite drops. So the food you eat has to be efficient. Maximum protein, minimum calories. So this is where usually things fall apart. Knowing this is easy, but doing this every day when you barely have any appetite, not so much. And that's where when smart nutrition comes in. Because smart nutrition doesn't fight the drug, it actually makes the drug work. So choose wisely.

tags.hook_line: India just handed 1.4 billion people an appetite‑suppressing drug.
tags.summary: Gayatri warns GLP‑1 users about protein intake and promotes smart nutrition to support the drug.

posts.creator: gayatrichona
posts.caption: High protein doesn’t always mean smart protein. If you’re not checking the math, we will.  Stay tuned for more reality checks.
posts.transcript: I make protein bars for a living and I'm here to tell you, you don't need to eat protein bars unless 15 grams of protein 17 grams of protein 20 grams of protein 20 grams of tasty protein Everyone today is flexing the amount of protein in grams right on the front of the pack 15, 20 and even 30 But no one's asking the simplest question You're getting into protein, but at what calorie cost? So today we're opening the curious case of protein efficiency The average protein bar in India gives you anywhere between 280 to 300 calories. Now let's put that into perspective. A paneer paratha is 320 calories. 150 grams of grilled chicken is anywhere between 220 to 250 calories. And a typical bowl of dal gives you 200 calories. So the real question isn't just how much protein, but it's actually how many calories are you eating just to get that protein. So if your bar that's actually meant to give you protein lands at 300 plus calories, then wouldn't you just rather eat a meal? So the next time you're picking your favorite protein bar, make sure not just to look at the protein content, but the calories that come with it.

tags.hook_line: I make protein bars for a living and I'm here to tell you, you don't need to eat protein bars unless…
tags.summary: The ad challenges viewers to evaluate protein bars by calorie cost versus whole‑food options.
